before: The suggestions-only policy refused a party's new row right above or below another person's pending new row as nested: it read each paragraph mark of the party's own new row as typed words at a caret, and the caret at its last cell's end read the next row's mark. It also refused a party's deletion that reached a control's prompt with another person's pending format on it, though the deletion leaves the prompt and the format as they were.
after: A new row beside another person's new row is beside it, as the host's check finds: what a new row, cell, table or note of the party's own holds lands with it. A deletion leaves a prompt's units, so the strike rule does not read them, and the deletion passes.
reason: The Yjs document format, the ordered protocol and the checkpoint manifest do not change. The policy runs the same code on every copy, and every copy of a room runs the same code version. Ordered rooms are not deployed yet.
